Source: A 36-year-old woman, G1P1001, presents to her gynecologist for an annual visit.
The patient’s mother had breast cancer at age 68, and her sister has endometriosis.
A pelvic exam reveals a non-tender, 12-week-size uterus with an irregular contour.
A transvaginal ultrasound is performed and demonstrates two intramural leiomyomas.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 138/74 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 13/min.
She states that she feels well and has no complaints.
She has a medical history of hypertension for which she takes hydrochlorothiazide.
